name: Domino Loo
description: Domino Loo is a trick-taking game for 2 to 4 players, adapted from the classic 17th-century card game Loo. It uses a standard set of double-six dominoes and features a unique trump-selection process along with a 'widow' hand called the Miss.

overview.description: Domino Loo is a trick-taking game for 2 to 4 players, adapted from the classic 17th-century card game Loo. It uses a standard set of double-six dominoes and features a unique trump-selection process along with a 'widow' hand called the Miss.

history.origins: Loo was a high-society gambling card game in the 17th century. The domino version emerged in the late 19th century, first documented in Berkeley's 'Dominoes and Solitaire' (1899).
timeline: 1600s: Card game Loo (originally Lanterloo) becomes popular in Europe.
1899: George Bell ('Berkeley') documents the domino adaptation.
Modern Era: Popular in 'Dealer's Choice' gaming nights as a variant of Boo-Ray.
history.cultural: Connected to the French game Lanterloo and the modern American game BourrÃ© (Boo-Ray).
history.evolution: The game moved from elite salons to lower-class gambling houses over three centuries, simplifying its rules while maintaining the 'Loo' penalty.

setup.dealing: Each player receives 5 tiles. A 'turn-up' tile is flipped from the boneyard to determine trumps.
setup.equipment: Dominoes and gaming chips for the pool.

rules.objective: Win as many tricks as possible to take a share of the pool. Avoid being 'Looed' (taking zero tricks).
rules.gameplay: 1. **Trumps**: The higher end of the turn-up tile is the trump suit. 2. **The Miss (Widow)**: In 3-4 player games, an extra hand of 5 tiles is dealt. Players can swap their hand for 'The Miss' or drop out. 3. **Dealer's Swap**: If the dealer keeps their hand, they can swap one tile for the turn-up trump tile. 4. **Trick Play**: Lead any tile. Must follow suit (if lead is a 5-2, the suit is 5). If unable to follow, must play a trump if held.
keyRules: Suit of a tile is determined by its ends. A 5-2 belongs to suit 5 and suit 2.
Only the first/second players to opt in can take the Miss.
Each trick won earns 1/5 of the pool.
Player who takes no tricks is 'Looed' and must pay penalty equal to original pool amount.

strategy.basic: If your hand lacks trumps or high-value doubles, drop out of the hand to avoid the Loo penalty.
strategy.intermediate: Taking the Miss is high-risk, high-reward. Use it if your current hand has only one low trump.
strategy.advanced: Dealer edge: Always use the swap to gain a trump unless your hand is already perfect (which is rare).
tips: In a 4-player game, pool distribution is tight; don't stay in without at least two decent trumps.
The 'Loo' penalty is severe - defensive passing is better than aggressive losing.
